newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen jumping after jobs.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen jumping after jobs.

text.p: U.S. stocks are seen bolting higher with bonds after the September jobs report came in much weaker than expected, analysts said. The following are their comments:
PHILIP ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT VALUE LINE ASSET MANAGEMENT:
-- "This is far weaker than expected. We could get to a Dow 6000 right here."
The long bond jumped 1-9/32, knocking its yield down to 6.73 percent. The December S&P 500 index futures contract climbed 3.60 to 701.30, indicating the Dow may open up about 28 points.
HUGH JOHNSON, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT FIRST ALBANY:

-- "It's very clear the economy slowed in September. It's obviously very good news for the Federal Reserve and for the bond market but a mixed blessing for stocks because it will intensify worries about earnings. The shift to the defensive side of the market will only increase."
-- "The two big surprises are the decline in manufacturing payrolls, hinted at by the Purchasing Managers index, and service sector payrolls up only 10,000. That is extraordinarily soft."
LARRY WACHTEL, ANALYST AT PRUDENTIAL SECURITIES:

-- "This is a vast surprise in terms of the announcement. Of course, August was overstated because the service week was longer. That was too strong. Now it's compensated with this decline. It is in keeping with other numbers. We have a softer economy. The Fed was addressing economic reality and not politics when it did not change rates."
-- Federal Reserve chairman Alan "Greenspan said there would be deceleration in the second half. It's another kudo for the fed which did not panic and held their fire."
